who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), lane: crates/blaze-program, merge-1113, round 5
where: crates/blaze-program/src/reach.rs (Reach, test_key), src/tests/world.rs (model_reach), src/walk.rs (new nodes in a tier-up walk)
what: A test's key was over the instance keys of the rows it reaches, and the oracle's model of what a test observes hashed the tier of each row. Both carried the tier, a quantity that changes no behaviour, and they disagreed on which rows: the oracle counted the tier of rows of instances the test only took in. Separately, a tier-up walk made a node new to the program at the fast tier, so the tier-up left a row that the next tier-up remakes.
cost: one compile-and-test round; a design decision (a tier-up must never rerun a test) the key did not hold
cause: an identity that holds more than the thing it identifies: the instance key is the identity of the code record, not of the behaviour a test observes; and a tier for new nodes fixed at Edit instead of derived from the delta
class: a key over a code identity used where a behaviour identity is meant (it moves on changes no reader can observe), and a default standing in for a rule
prevention: a test key is over tier-free plan keys of every instance a test can run, placed or taken in (FnRow::plan, FnRow::inlined with plan keys); the oracle reads the model only; the tier of a new node is Delta::new_at, stated in the row rule
fix: reach.rs over (Symbol, PlanKey) of rows and their inline closures; Walked/FnRow carry plan keys; WalkConfig::new_at and Delta::new_at; model_reach drops the tier
state: fixed, unverified until the main agent runs the tests
